notes: Clear single message: app icon, large title, three benefit rows, one primary CTA.
Full-width hairline above the footer (page dots + CTA) reads more web/Material than Apple onboarding; drop it or use a fade.
Hero glyph is a car, not the barrier; fine, but the About app icon uses an 'M010 + striped arm' mark, so the brand mark differs between the two places.
Large empty band between benefits and footer (~200 pt); acceptable for onboarding.
Empty state is clear: Bluetooth glyph, title, one-sentence explanation, full-width primary 'Connect to barrier'.
Empty state + CTA use a different composition from Health's disconnected state (centered-low with full-width button here, top-aligned with hugging button on Health). Pick one empty-state component.
Status chips sit under the large title here but inline with the title on Health; header layout is inconsistent between the two tabs.
State reads instantly: green hero tint, flat arm, 'Lowered' + 'Arm is flat. You can drive in.'
Lower disabled with 'Already lowered.' hint; Raise primary. Good affordance.
Thumb-zone action dock (hint line, Lower/Raise, full-width STOP) is good; arrows + words, not color-only.
Header subtitle 'M010-Barrier · Signed in 0.53 s · phone-measured' is engineering copy on the driver screen, and the two middle-dot separators are spaced differently.
Roughly 150 pt of dead background between the status chips and the action dock; the screen feels top-heavy. Consider anchoring chips to the dock or giving the hero a little more height.
Idle STOP is a pale red tinted pill that is visually close to a disabled control; make it clear STOP is always live (e.g. outline + solid icon) or explain that it only matters while moving.
Best state on the screen set: blue hero, angled arm, 'Raising', elapsed '0.8 s of about 4.0 s' + progress bar; STOP becomes solid red and Lower/Raise lock with 'Arm is moving. Use Stop.'
Dead band between chips and the dock still present (see control-lowered).
Header subtitle is engineering copy (see control-lowered).
State clear: vertical arm, 'Raised', 'Arm is up. Your space is reserved.' Lower becomes green primary, Raise disabled with 'Already raised.'
Thumb-zone action dock (hint line, Lower/Raise, full-width STOP) is good; arrows + words, not color-only.
Header subtitle 'M010-Barrier · Signed in 0.53 s · phone-measured' is engineering copy on the driver screen, and the two middle-dot separators are spaced differently.
Roughly 150 pt of dead background between the status chips and the action dock; the screen feels top-heavy. Consider anchoring chips to the dock or giving the hero a little more height.
Idle STOP is a pale red tinted pill that is visually close to a disabled control; make it clear STOP is always live (e.g. outline + solid icon) or explain that it only matters while moving.
Amber hero, mid-angle arm, 'Stopped' + 'Raise or lower to continue.'; both directions enabled. Clear.
No hint line above the buttons in this state (other states have one), so the dock top edge jumps; keep a one-line hint slot for a stable layout.
Header subtitle 'M010-Barrier · Signed in 0.53 s · phone-measured' is engineering copy on the driver screen, and the two middle-dot separators are spaced differently.
Roughly 150 pt of dead background between the status chips and the action dock; the screen feels top-heavy. Consider anchoring chips to the dock or giving the hero a little more height.
Idle STOP is a pale red tinted pill that is visually close to a disabled control; make it clear STOP is always live (e.g. outline + solid icon) or explain that it only matters while moving.
Refusal banner is plain-language ('Something is in the way' + how to fix) with a 'Safety checks' drill-in and a dismiss X; the 'Zone blocked' chip carries an icon, not color only.
Banner sits 8 pt above Lower/Raise while the rest of the screen uses 24 pt rhythm; the dock feels cramped. Add 16 pt below the banner.

Hero still says 'Lowered / Arm is flat. You can drive in.' in green while the zone is blocked; this is literally true but reads optimistic next to an amber refusal. Consider a secondary line on the hero ('Zone blocked') when a guard is active.
'Safety checks >' link is ~17 pt text; make sure the hit area spans the full banner width or at least 44 pt tall.

Fault is unmistakable: red hero, warning glyph + 'Fault', dashed ghost arm, 'Sensors: see fault' chip, and a 'Needs on-site reset' card with the exact recovery action ('Hold the unit button for 8 seconds').
'Controls locked.' hint but STOP looks identical to idle STOP; say explicitly whether STOP still works in FAULT (the presenter scenario says it does).
Fault card body uses label color at body size while the hero subtitle uses secondary; minor type-weight inconsistency.
Neutral white hero, dashed ghost arm, 'Position unknown' + 'Lower it to home the barrier.'; Lower is the only enabled direction. Clear.
Small '?' glyph floats alone at the top of the hero above the arm; it looks like a tappable help icon. Either make it a real help button or move it next to the title like the Fault glyph.
Hint 'Lower first to confirm position' lacks the trailing period used by the other hints ('Already lowered.').
Header subtitle 'M010-Barrier · Signed in 0.53 s · phone-measured' is engineering copy on the driver screen, and the two middle-dot separators are spaced differently.
Roughly 150 pt of dead background between the status chips and the action dock; the screen feels top-heavy. Consider anchoring chips to the dock or giving the hero a little more height.
Connection-lost banner with a primary Reconnect, a greyed 'Last known: Raising / Not live.' hero and clock-badged stale chips: the offline state is clear and actionable.

BUG: the stale chips row (Zone clear / Sensors OK / 12.90 V) is cut through the middle by the action-dock top edge in the first viewport. Reserve space so the chips fit above the dock, or drop them in this state.
'Connection lost' appears twice (red chip and banner title) within 100 pt; let the chip say 'Offline' or hide it while the banner is shown.
STOP is fully disabled here; correct for an offline phone, and the hint 'Controls are off while offline.' explains it.
Native sheet: Close at top right, large title, grouped 'NEARBY BARRIERS' row with BT avatar, 'Previously paired' pill, signal bars and chevron; 'Scan again' text button; local-only footnote.
Signal-strength bars have no text equivalent visible (add an accessibility label such as 'Strong signal').
Only the found-device state is captured; no scanning or 'none found' state to judge.
Grouped inset lists (Barrier / Safety interlocks / Power) with section headers; values right-aligned; check icons + words for interlocks.
'Barrier's last counter' is protocol jargon for a driver-facing tab; move to This barrier/advanced or explain it.
Header chips inline with the large title here, under the title on Barrier: inconsistent header pattern between sibling tabs.
Power card's '12900 mV' line is cut by the tab bar at the fold; fine since it scrolls, but the hero 12.90 V reads as one big number with no label until you scroll.
Clear empty state with icon, title, explanation and CTA.
CTA is a hugging button here but full-width on the Barrier tab; empty state sits high here but low on Barrier. Unify the empty-state component.
Segmented filter (All / Commands / Auth / Faults), collapsible evidence summary, grouped list with icons; destructive 'Clear log' in red at the end.
'Share CSV' is a large tinted pill in the large-title row; an Apple-native pattern would be a share icon in the nav bar. It also pulls focus from the title.
Row metadata ('00:59:26.188 · Lower · #3 · 70 ms · simulated') is dense and repeats 'simulated' on every row; consider showing that once in the summary.
Event titles mix styles: 'Lower: Moving' vs 'State Lowering' (no colon) vs 'Owner authorized in 543 ms'. Pick one pattern.
Evidence summary wraps leaving '0.54 s' orphaned on its own line.
No empty state captured (e.g. a filter with no events).
Classic grouped settings: Connection segmented with locked Bluetooth + explanation, This barrier row, Appearance segmented, Haptics switch, General nav rows with tinted icon tiles.

Segmented controls are wrapped inside a white card with its own padding (card-in-card); on iOS a segmented control sits directly in the group or as the row itself. Removes ~30 pt of chrome per section.
The lock glyph on 'Bluetooth' is good; the disabled reason is explained in the footer.
Scenario list grouped by Motion / Safety interlocks with step count and FSM row chips; Exit presenter pinned at the bottom.
Back label '< Settings' is tight to the chevron here but '<  Back' on onboarding has a much wider gap; unify the back-button component.
Cards with multi-line body + chips + chevron are dense; acceptable for a presenter tool.
Two radio-style cards; unavailable Bluetooth option is dimmed with a lock and the reason inline; selected card has accent border + check. Clear.
Back button: chevron-to-label gap (~18 pt) is much wider than the '< Settings' back buttons elsewhere.
Unavailable card keeps a grey 1 pt border while the rest of the app is borderless; consider dropping it.
Standard pre-permission prompt: icon tile, title, why-copy, primary 'Allow Bluetooth' and secondary 'Not now'.
Back button spacing inconsistency as on onboarding-mode.
~330 pt of empty space between copy and footer; acceptable for a permission primer.
Three numbered step cards with a 1:00 'not started' ring and a primary 'Start 60 s timer'.
Step 1 says 'Tap Start' but the button says 'Start 60 s timer', and step 3 says 'Tap Connect' but no Connect control exists on this screen yet; align copy with the actual controls.
Step 3 trailing icon is a keypad, which suggests entering a code rather than connecting.
Step text is set in a medium/semibold weight at body size, which reads heavy next to the regular-weight subtitle.
Success tile, 'You're all set.', next-step guidance, single CTA.
'Connect to barrier' inside the sentence is not distinguished (quote or bold it) so the instruction is easy to miss.
Large empty band above the footer; acceptable.
Grouped details list, explanatory footer, separate destructive 'Forget this barrier' group with consequence text. Textbook iOS.
Two counter rows are protocol details; acceptable here because the footer explains them, but they could live under a disclosure.
App icon, name, team line, version, privacy group: clean.

Step pills are left-aligned with a ragged right edge; center them or let them stretch.
Chip text 'FSM rows 7' / 'FSM rows 11' should be singular when one row is listed.
Bottom toolbar has two icon-only buttons (reset, sliders); give them accessibility labels (acceptable for presenter use).
'As expected' badge, checklist of result/state/guard mask, what the driver sees. Good evidence layout.
